lens:
ODDS OF AVERAGING CAD 5k/MONTH BY MONTH 3 (about Dec 2026 – Jan 2027). I weighed four things: (1) built-in distribution with buyer intent that works without the owner, and whether money can buy volume inside 90 days; (2) willingness to pay (price per customer sets how many customers are needed); (3) time to approval, first dollar and cash in the bank (store review, unmonetized launch periods, payout holds); (4) base rates.

SCALE: scores use the same absolute scale as the verifiers' p5k_90d (1.0 ≈ a 10% chance). They are ESTIMATES made with judgment, not measurements. Where a dossier and its adversarial verification disagreed, I used the verification.

HEADLINE: no candidate has an evidence-based chance above about 2–5%, and none can be guaranteed. The hard ceiling for any single new product is below about 5%. Averaging US$5k/month over 3 months means at least $15k cumulative, and RevenueCat's '$10k cumulative within 2 years' milestone is reached by only about 1 in 20 subscription apps (cross_baserates.json). Other anchors: the TrustMRR year-0 median is US$148 MRR (n=5,079, opt-in and biased upward), only 0.9% of products are 'breaking out', and survivors took a median 8 months to reach US$1K MRR (cand_saas.json, via cross_baserates.json). The owner's no-audience, no-posting constraint makes these published base rates optimistic for this case (cross_baserates.json conclusion 4, which is a judgment).

ranking.candidate: cand_aichat — vertical AI web app; best niche is a CELPIP/IELTS-General-style writing and speaking practice grader sold as one-time passes
ranking.reason:
Best fit to this lens, and still a long shot: the verifier puts it well under 2% (judgment).

FOR:
- Highest consumer willingness to pay in the bundle. Deadline-driven buyers pay C$39 for a 30-day pass (net C$31.18) or C$79 for 90 days (net C$59.93) (dossier ESTIMATE). Comparable apps charge Speak $20/month and Duolingo Max $29.99/month.
- Quickest route to cash. It is a web app with no store review. Stripe's first payout comes 7–14 days after the first payment (Canada: 7 days, Stripe doc mirror), so first money in November is plausible.
- Paid search is the one channel where money can buy intent traffic inside 90 days.
- Buyers are mostly Canada-based, so plain Stripe Canada works without EU or Korean VAT. Selling to Canada only is my inference from cross_payments.json.

AGAINST (from the verification):
- The daily free check makes this freemium, not a hard paywall, so conversion is 2.1% rather than 10.7%.
- Passes do not stack like subscriptions. It needs about 168–197 NEW buyers every month.
- A capped ad budget of C$20–30/day buys about 300–900 clicks at C$1–2 CPC [prior knowledge, unverified]. That is about 5–24 payers a month.
- Advertising on the 'CELPIP' trademark may be restricted [prior knowledge].
- A direct competitor exists: CELPIPAce offers AI scoring and a paid tier.
- Calibrating the grader needs human-rated ground truth.
- Anthropic's Usage Policy lists 'Academic testing' as high-risk, which requires professional review (cross_payments.json). It must be framed as practice feedback only, and that needs checking.

ESTIMATE of the ad economics: buyers needed = 5,234 / (31.18 − CAC). At a CAC of C$10 that is 247 buyers and C$2.5k of ads a month. At C$20 it is 468 buyers and C$9.4k of ads. At C$25 it is 847 buyers and C$21k. Actual CELPIP CPC: not found.

Month-3 net ESTIMATE: C$0–1,000 (verifier).

ranking.candidate: cand_marketplace — one Shopify App Store app (Atlassian Forge hedge dropped)
ranking.reason:
FOR:
- Buyers already search the store with intent, and billing is built in (Shopify Billing API).
- 0% revenue share on the first US$1M lifetime (secondary).
- B2B prices mean the fewest customers of any candidate: about 136–209 merchants at US$29.99–19.99, or about 335 once the AI cost of non-converting trial installs is counted (verifier ESTIMATE).

AGAINST:
- Review takes 1–4 weeks, so the listing lands around Oct 30 – Nov 20.
- Merchants 'don't want to touch their stores' over Christmas (Genlook anecdote), which is exactly the launch window.
- It needs 10–31 installs a day for about 68 days (verifier ESTIMATE).
- Install→paid rates are not published by any platform.
- The best 2026 comparable (Genlook) reached about US$700 MRR after 2–3 months, with manual prospecting: about 19% of the target.
- A US$180-lifetime quit case and 35% of apps with zero reviews point the same way.
- First cash arrives Dec–Jan.

Verifier: ≤1% chance. Better as a 6–12 month asset than a month-3 bet.

ranking.candidate: cand_digital — Etsy-first digital templates and planners
ranking.reason:
FOR:
- The only candidate with a large built-in buyer marketplace: Etsy had 88.5M active buyers (10-Q, Mar 2025).
- It has a seasonal tailwind inside the window (Dec–Jan planners) [prior knowledge].

AGAINST:
- Low price: it needs 243–808 sales a month. That is over 30× the average Etsy seller (US$142/month ESTIMATE from the 10-Q) and over 30× the TrustMRR year-0 median.
- The only autonomous-AI analog (Gumroad_AI) made €0 in 14 weeks.
- Etsy's 'human touch' and 'original prompts' rules require real creative work from the owner. Buyer messages, ads and refunds are dashboard-only. Setup is 17–23 h (verifier), which breaks the owner-time constraint.
- The Etsy API key approval is a single point of failure.

January ESTIMATE: C$0–1,000 gross, most likely near the bottom of that range.

ranking.candidate: cand_mobile — iOS hard-paywall subscription app (Expo) with Apple Search Ads
ranking.reason:
FOR:
- A hard paywall converts 10.7% vs 2.1% for freemium, and iOS converts 2.6% vs 0.9% on Google Play (RevenueCat 2026, secondary).
- Search ads can buy installs.

AGAINST:
- It needs about 506 subscribers (US$5,058 gross).
- Ads to reach that cost about CAD 8k–41k a month (verifier), and paid acquisition breaks even or loses money.
- Review takes 1–4 weeks, and submissions rose 60–80% in Q1 2026.
- Apple pays within 45 days after the fiscal month closes, so December revenue becomes cash around February. That fails a 'by January' average.
- The median app earns US$72/month at 12 months.

Verifier: well under 1–2% for the Dec–Jan window.

ranking.candidate: cand_bots — Telegram Stars group-assistant bot (Discord and Kakao ruled out)
ranking.reason:
FOR:
- Owner-light, and installs spread inside groups.

AGAINST:

- It needs about 786–2,860 paying groups, from 26k–95k active groups (verifier ESTIMATE).

- Telegram's native translation and summaries compete with it [prior knowledge].
- Cash timing: Stars are withdrawable 21 days after receipt (secondary), with a 1,000-Star minimum, and pay out in TON crypto. Whether a Canadian exchange can sell TON: not found. December cash comes from November sales.

Verifier: ≤3% chance, CAD 0–100 typical at month 3. My lens marks it down further for cash lag and zero conversion data.

AGAINST:

- The one comparable launch had zero external traffic.

Verifier: 1–3% for one peak month, under 1% for a sustained average.

ranking.candidate: cand_seo — programmatic SEO / calculator site on AdSense
ranking.reason:
Worst fit:
- Only 1.74% of new pages reach the top 10 within a year (Ahrefs, 2026-04 update).
- 4 of 4 AI-built analogs were rejected by AdSense for 'Low value content', at 6–150 sessions a month.

- Cash in the bank inside the window: about CAD 0 (verifier).

recommended_strategy:
RECOMMEND ONE PRIMARY PRODUCT ON ONE WEB STACK, not a broad portfolio. At most, add low-cost extra shots that reuse the same accounts. Several AI-built products do not, on this evidence, add up to C$5k by January:
- Every candidate has a per-shot chance of about 0.5–1%.
- The shots are correlated: same owner, no audience, the same slow or paid channels.
- Each new store or marketplace eats owner setup hours.
- ESTIMATE (cross_baserates.json): 10 independent shots at 0.5–1% give about 5–10%, and correlation pushes that lower.
- Summing five products at $1k each: under 5% even with generous assumptions.
- The ≤10 h setup budget is used up by a single web product: 7.25–10.75 h per the aichat verifier.

PRIMARY: a web (not app-store) AI writing and speaking practice tool for Canadian-immigration English tests. Name it descriptively (for example 'CLB writing & speaking practice'), not 'CELPIP' or 'official'.
- Stack: the repo's Next.js 16 app (read node_modules/next/dist/docs first, per AGENTS.md) on Cloudflare Workers, the Claude API (Sonnet 5 grading with a cached rubric; Batch for non-urgent work), and Stripe Canada.
- Sales: Canada-only, so plain Stripe works without foreign-VAT registration (cross_payments.json). GST/HST is irrelevant below $30k (ETA s.148).
- Pricing: hard paywall after exactly 1 free graded writing task and 1 free speaking task (no daily free checks). C$39 30-day pass (net C$31.18), C$79 90-day pass (net C$59.93).
- Channel: Google/Microsoft search ads on non-trademark intent terms at an owner-approved cap of C$20–30/day, plus 2–3 substantive guide pages a week and a 30% referral program for tutors (CASL-compliant).
- Kill and scale rules, all owner-approved:
  - Scale spend only if measured CAC stays at or below about C$10–15 for 14 days. ESTIMATE: buyers needed = 5,234 / (31.18 − CAC), so a CAC of C$10 means 247 buyers and about C$2.5k/month of ads.
  - Stop ads if CAC exceeds first-sale net (about C$31) for 14 days.
  - Nov 30 go/pivot memo: under C$500 net in November with no rising trend means stop or pivot.

GATES BEFORE BUILDING PAYMENTS:
- (a) Gate 0 from the decision memo: the owner's legal right to be self-employed, and EI filed by 2026-10-10 with the Service Canada 'minor extent' question asked.
- (b) The AI re-reads Anthropic's current Usage Policy and confirms a practice-feedback grader is outside the high-risk 'Academic testing' category. If it is not clearly outside, switch to a non-exam niche on the same stack.
- (c) The owner can fund C$1.4–2.1k of ads over about 10 weeks (dossier ESTIMATE), on top of about C$800–1,100 of fixed costs over 3 months (verifier ESTIMATE). Without ad money, the only fast channel is gone and the odds fall to base-rate levels.

OPTIONAL EXTRA SHOT, only if setup hours remain: one Shopify App Store app, run as a 6–12 month asset. The holiday freeze and review lag make it near-irrelevant to the January number.

DO NOT add a Korean saju New Year product unless Stripe clears the category in writing: Polar prohibits it, and Stripe's position is not found.

HONEST FRAMING: this is the best-odds option in the bundle, not a likely route to C$5k.
- Chance of averaging C$5k/month by Dec–Jan: about 1–2% (ESTIMATE, judgment; verifier: well under 2%).
- Realistic month-3 net: C$0–1,000 (verifier).
- The owner needs a separate income floor: EI and/or the home-services fallback already in decision-memo.md.

notes:
WHAT CANNOT BE GUARANTEED: no strategy in the bundle has evidence of averaging CAD 5k/month by Dec 2026 – Jan 2027 for an owner with no audience who does not post.
- Every verifier's adjusted p5k_90d is between 0.1 and 0.5.
- The hard ceiling for any single new product is below about 5% (RevenueCat: $10k cumulative within 2 years ≈ 1 in 20 apps, secondary). My judgment for the recommended primary is about 1–2%.
- Scores above are ESTIMATES on the verifiers' absolute scale. The differences between candidates are small and rest on judgment about timing, willingness to pay and channel. They are not measured probabilities.

WHY aichat NARROWLY BEATS Shopify through this lens: time to first dollar. A web app has no store review, and Stripe's first Canadian payout comes about 7 days after the first charge (secondary doc mirror). Paid search can be bought now, while the Shopify listing lands in the holiday freeze (Genlook anecdote), install→paid rates are unpublished, and merchant billing delays cash. Shopify needs fewer customers (B2B price), so it is the better 6–12 month asset, not a better January bet.

THE ONE LEVER THAT MATERIALLY CHANGES THE ODDS is capital for paid acquisition, and only after a capped test proves CAC well below first-sale net.
- cross_distribution.json ESTIMATE: 500 payers cost US$8k–26k at median CPI with a hard paywall; year-1 LTV of $32 covers only 0.62–1.71x of that CAC.
- The owner's savings are unknown and decisive.
- A second lever, owner community posting (Korean-Canadian and newcomer groups), is excluded by the owner's constraint, yet every fast success in the evidence used founder-led distribution.

OPERATOR RISKS TO CARRY INTO THE BUILD (cross_operator.json):
- Routines: hourly minimum interval; 5 runs/day on Pro, 15 on Max (secondary); they cannot approve pending actions; double-fire bugs are listed in the CHANGELOG.
- This environment blocks api.stripe.com and api.cloudflare.com. Put secrets and deploys in GitHub Actions, and monitor outcomes rather than job status: this repo's scraper stayed green for 46 days while collecting 0 prices.
- The repo is PUBLIC and exposes the owner's EI plans. Recommend making it private.
- The Claude plan that runs the Routines (US$20–200/month, prior knowledge) is a real fixed cost that most dossiers left out.

UNKNOWNS THAT COULD FLIP THE RANKING:
- CELPIP/CLB keyword CPC and test-taker volume (not found).
- Whether Google Ads restricts immigration-test-prep advertisers or the trademark.
- The owner's English level, which limits spot-checking graded outputs.
- Shopify install→paid rates (not published).

lens: HANDS-OFF & CAPITAL. The question: which strategy needs the least owner time after a setup of 10 h or less, and puts the least money at risk for an owner who needs income? I penalised hidden owner labour (sales, posting, support, content, uploads), ad budgets, and legal or platform risk (regulated advice, spam or ToS problems, store or processor bans, crypto cash-out). Where a dossier and its adversarial verification disagreed, I used the verification's hours, cash and scores. Weights (my judgement): owner hours 40%, cash at risk 30%, legal/platform risk 30%. Revenue odds counted only as a tiebreaker: cash spent on a product that earns about $0 is lost cash.

ranking.candidate: cand_apiagents: Apify Store pay-per-event (PPE) Actor portfolio sub-variant only
ranking.reason: Least hidden labour of the options that have a built-in paying market. Apify handles billing, tax and discovery, so no merchant of record (MoR) and no foreign VAT registration. Creators get 80% of revenue minus platform costs, paid monthly with a US$20 minimum via PayPal/Wise after KYC (official apify-docs). Verified owner time: setup 8.5–10 h, weekly 0.75–1.5 h. No ad budget. Verified 3-month cash: CAD 113–1,077, most of it the Claude plan that runs the Routines. Penalties: (1) Rental pricing retires 2026-10-01 (official _rental-sunsetting.mdx), so PPE is the only model left. (2) Agentic-payment eligibility means the creator absorbs proxy and browser costs, so avoid bot-protected targets. (3) Scraping ToS and PIPEDA risk: the verifier says the named Korean e-commerce niche has unresearched legal exposure, and the Canadian public-data niches compete with free official feeds. (4) The 14-day issue-response rule means the business is never fully hands-off. Verified month-3 revenue: CAD 0–100 realistic, CAD 150–550 optimistic. p5k 0.2/10.

ranking.candidate: cand_seo: programmatic SEO / free web-tools site with ads
ranking.reason: Lowest cash of any candidate: CAD 20–100 up front, then CAD 0–10/month plus the Claude plan (dossier, verified). No ad spend. It can run on Cloudflare Pages from this existing repo. The verifier raised owner time to 9–12 h setup (Google Cloud service account, AdSense ID and mailed PIN) and 1–1.5 h/week (contact inbox, PIPEDA duties). It pays nothing until AdSense approves the site: 4 of 4 AI-built analogues were rejected for 'low value content'. Verified month-3 revenue: USD 0–5, p5k 0.1/10. The recommended YMYL variant (EI/CPP/HST calculators) puts Competition Act s.52 liability on an owner who cannot audit the outputs, and its parameters sit on canada.ca, which this environment's network blocks. cross_payments says auto-published AI media needs human review under Anthropic's policy, which is more hidden labour. Very hands-off, but it does almost nothing toward income.

ranking.candidate: cand_extension: one freemium Chrome extension
ranking.reason: Low cash: verified CAD 150–1,250 over 3 months including the Claude plan. No ads required. Store updates can be published by API from GitHub Actions. Verified owner time is 8.5–10.5 h setup (at the ceiling) and about 2 h/week on average, rising to 3–5 h in rejection or appeal weeks. New listings, the Privacy tab, review replies and appeals are dashboard-only work for the owner. The trader declaration publicly shows the owner's name, phone and address, so a virtual mailbox is needed. Free-tier AI calls can run up API bills unless hard caps or on-device AI are used; the verifier also showed Cloudflare Free KV limits fail at scale, so Workers Paid is needed. Platform risk: an opaque takedown can spread to the owner's other Google services. Realistic need is 80k–120k active users (verifier), so income odds are about 0; p5k 0.2/10.

ranking.candidate: cand_marketplace: single Shopify app (drop app #2 and the Forge hedge)
ranking.reason: Billing is built in (Billing API) with 0% share on the first US$1M, so no MoR and little cash. Verified 3-month cash is CAD 550–1,500 including the Claude plan; ads are optional. The verifier found the full plan needs 12–14 h of setup, over budget; one app is about 9.75 h. Weekly work is 1.3–2.1 h, but incident weeks run 5–8 h: merchant support is in English, and one storefront-breaking bug brings 1-star reviews. Review rounds need the owner to relay messages. Listing lands in the BFCM/holiday freeze. Every documented fast Shopify success used founder outreach, which this owner excludes. Month-3 revenue C$0–300 (verifier). p5k 0.5/10.

ranking.reason: On paper it is owner-light: verified owner_light 7, 1–2 h/week, 8–10 h setup, and cash of CAD 314–961 including an accountant, with no ads. ranking.reason: Minimum cash is CAD 250–450 (Apple US$99/yr and others). The recommended plan adds an Apple Search Ads budget that the verifier recomputed to CAD 900–2,700. recommended_strategy:
Verdict: no candidate is a way to earn income by Jan 2027. Every verifier rates the chance of reaching CAD 5k at 0.1–0.5/10. cross_baserates puts one product with no audience at about 1% or lower (judgement), and a 10–20-shot portfolio at about 5–20% at best, because the shots share the same weaknesses. So under this lens the owner's income floor must stay outside these products: the decision-memo plan, with the EI claim filed by 2026-10-10 and home services. Treat any AI-run online product as a capped side experiment. Nothing about its revenue can be guaranteed.

If the owner still wants one: run exactly ONE no-ad shot for the first 90 days, an Apify Store PPE Actor portfolio.
- Scope: 8–15 Actors, pay-per-event only. Rental pricing is blocked for new Actors and retires 2026-10-01.
- Pricing: about US$1–10 per 1,000 results, the range Apify's academy gives for most Store prices.
- Sources: only official or open APIs, or sites whose terms allow automated access. No personal data. No bot-protected Korean e-commerce (Coupang/Naver). No residential-proxy targets, because under PPE agentic eligibility the creator absorbs platform costs.
- Operations: Claude builds in GitHub, deploys through GitHub Actions and drafts issue replies within Apify's 14-day rule. The owner approves.

Owner time (verified ESTIMATE): 8.5–10 h setup. That covers a dedicated business email, Apify Creator plan (US$1/month) with ID/KYC, PayPal or Wise, an Anthropic key with a hard spend cap of about US$50, GitHub secrets, network allowlisting, and the Claude plan for Routines. Then 0.75–1.5 h/week.

Cash at risk (ESTIMATE): 3 months × US$20–100 Claude plan × 1.37 = CAD 82–411, plus CAD 27–205 of API and about CAD 4 for Apify, ≈ CAD 113–620. The verifier's all-in range is CAD 113–1,077. Ad spend: $0.

Channel: Apify Store search, Apify's MCP server with x402/Skyfire agent payments, the Make/n8n/Zapier integrations, and GitHub README pages.

Kill rule (dossier/verifier): under US$100/month of paid usage by end of Jan 2027 → maintenance only.

Expected month-3 revenue (verifier): CAD 0–100, optimistic CAD 150–550.

Optional second shot, only if setup hours remain: a small non-YMYL free-tools section on this repo's existing static Next.js export, on Cloudflare Pages. No AdSense until at least 20 substantive pages. No mass pages. Cash is about CAD 20–100, and it shares the same Claude plan.

Before launching anything: call Service Canada. Under EI Regs s.30, a business that is more than 'minor in extent' can zero EI in every operating week, even when AI does the work (cross_payments). At the ESTIMATE maximum benefit of B = $729/week, that is 729 × 52 / 12 ≈ $3,159/month at risk. That is far larger than any setup cost, and a multi-product portfolio makes 'minor' harder to argue.

lens: AI build and operate leverage. For each candidate I asked three questions. (1) Can Claude get it to launch-ready in this session, meaning code, payment integration in test mode, content, legal pages, store or listing assets and CI? (2) Can Routines (hourly at most, stateless, 5 runs/day on Pro or 15 on Max per secondary sources, and unable to approve pending actions: cross_operator) plus GitHub Actions run it afterwards? That covers deploys, content and SEO pages, fixes, experiments and analytics digests. (3) How much is left to a human that the AI cannot do: store review loops, dashboard-only actions, uploads, owner-account posting, KYC and payouts? A candidate loses points in proportion to those human-only steps. Two facts about this environment shaped every score. First, this session's egress blocks api.stripe.com, api.cloudflare.com, play.google.com and developer.chrome.com (first-hand test in cross_operator). That means the AI can write and test code here, but live deploys and API calls must go through GitHub Actions secrets or an owner allowlist. Second, the repo is already a Next.js 16 static export aimed at Cloudflare Pages (next.config.ts: output 'export'). A web product reuses that stack directly. Leverage does not create demand. Every dossier and verification agrees that distribution, not building, is the binding constraint (cross_baserates, cross_distribution), so a high score here means 'cheapest to build and run', not 'likely to earn'.

ranking.candidate: cand_aichat: vertical AI web app with paywall (Claude API, Cloudflare Workers, merchant of record)
ranking.reason: Best fit for this lens. It is plain web code on the repo's existing Next.js and Cloudflare path, so there is no app-store review and no human review queue. The AI can build the whole thing this session: magic-link auth, D1, merchant-of-record checkout plus webhooks in test mode, rubric prompts with a cached prefix, the free-tool funnel, legal and CASL pages, and the KPI digest. Afterwards it deploys, publishes guide pages, runs A/B tests from config, drafts support replies and prepares ad files through Actions and Routines. API cost is small next to price: US$2.21/month for a typical CELPIP-style user on Sonnet 5 (dossier arithmetic, checked by the verifier). The verifier cut ai_build to 7 and ai_operate to 5 for three reasons: calibrated scoring needs human-rated ground truth; ad bid management stays owner labour until Google approves an API developer token [prior knowledge, unverified, pre-2026-06]; and setup realistically takes 7.25–10.75 h. I score it 8 anyway because it is the only consumer candidate with no platform gatekeeper between a git push and a paying customer. The verifier puts P(C$5k) at well under 2%.

ranking.candidate: cand_bots: Telegram group-assistant bot sold for Telegram Stars
ranking.reason: Very AI-operable. The Bot API, Stars invoices and subscriptions, refundStarPayment, getStarTransactions and the Mini App are all documented and callable from a Cloudflare Worker, with no store review for a plain bot. Support, refunds, A/B price tests and KPI commits can all run without a human. The deductions: the bot and its Stars balance sit on the owner's personal Telegram account, which is a single point of failure. Withdrawals go only through Fragment to TON with the owner's 2FA, and whether a Canadian-registered exchange sells TON was not found. The affiliate lever may be switched off for the account (starref_program_allowed=false in the example config). Setup adds wallet and exchange KYC; the verifier's estimate is 8–10 h.

ranking.candidate: cand_seo: programmatic SEO / free calculator site with ads
ranking.reason: The easiest thing here for the AI to build, since it is a static export on Cloudflare Pages Free, and the Search Console API can feed the Routines. It loses leverage on the operating side. The yearly and monthly parameters live on canada.ca, which is egress-blocked here (verification). AdSense approval, re-review and appeals are human steps. Anthropic's usage policy lists auto-published 'media' content as a high-risk use needing professional review (cross_payments). Most of all, the leverage turns into nothing: month-3 revenue is USD 0–4.80 when re-anchored to comparable AI-built sites (verification ESTIMATE). It is useful only as the content layer of a paid product, not as a business of its own.

ranking.candidate: cand_newsletter: AI-written paid newsletter on Ghost
ranking.reason: The recurring loop is the most automatable of all: the Ghost Admin API publishes and emails to free or paid segments without a human (official TryGhost docs, verified). Deductions: it is unclear which Ghost(Pro) tier allows custom integrations and paid members (not found). Source hosts are blocked, so the fetchers must run in Actions. Anthropic's usage policy classes auto-published journalistic content as high-risk and requiring human review (cross_payments), which conflicts with 'owner does nothing'. The immigration-news variant also needs English-source fact review by an owner whose English level is unknown, plus care around IRPA s.91. Month-3 revenue without ads is about C$9–140 (verification ESTIMATE).

ranking.candidate: cand_apiagents: Apify pay-per-event Actors, API and agent marketplaces
ranking.reason: Actors, CI push, pay-per-event charging and health checks are all code, and Apify handles billing and payouts; its fee and payout terms come from its official docs. The verifier found that the rental model, one of the dossier's routes to the target, is dead: new rental Actors have been blocked since 2026-04-01 and rental retires on 2026-10-01 (official _rental-sunsetting.mdx). Scrapers break without warning, and a failing Actor is flagged 'under maintenance' after 3 days. Replies to user Issues may have to be pasted by the owner (not verified). Legality sign-off for Korean and Canadian scraping targets is human judgement. The assistant-store sub-channels pay Canadian builders nothing, with Poe the only exception, and Poe has no earnings evidence.

Every version goes through review (budget 1–3 weeks, secondary), so weekly experiments are not feasible; the verifier's estimate is about 3–8 releases by the end of December. Review replies and stats are dashboard-bound. The CWS store is blocked from this sandbox for niche validation. A paid listing publishes the trader's name and address.

ranking.candidate: cand_digital: Etsy / Gumroad digital products
ranking.reason: The Etsy Open API v3 can create, upload and publish listings, and the AI can generate PDF and XLSX products. Buyer messages, Etsy Ads and refunds have no API, and the AI cannot even read buyer messages. Etsy's Creativity Standards require 'a seller's original prompts' and 'a human touch', which means ongoing creative work by the owner. The verifier's estimate of launch QA plus setup is 17–23 owner hours, over the 10 h budget. Seller-app key approval is a single point of failure resting on one third-party source. An AI-run Gumroad store analogue made €0 in 14 weeks.

ranking.candidate: cand_mobile: Expo / React Native subscription app
ranking.reason: EAS cloud builds remove the need for a Mac (official Expo docs), and RevenueCat plus OTA updates are scriptable. The AI still cannot run the iOS simulator or test camera and StoreKit flows on a device, so the owner has to do TestFlight checks. App Review rejections take multiple rounds (a 2026 AI app was rejected twice, about 4 weeks), and Resolution Center replies are probably manual [prior knowledge, unverified]. The owner must accept Apple agreements and handle 2FA prompts. Android needs 12 real testers for 14 days. This is the native-store penalty this lens is meant to apply.

ranking.candidate: cand_korea: Korea-market AI products (saju and similar), sold from Canada
ranking.reason: The code is buildable: a deterministic 만세력 engine plus Stripe with Korean payment methods. But the go/no-go gates are human and may never resolve. Stripe's approval of the fortune category, and whether a Canadian account can use Korean payment methods, were not found. Polar prohibits fortune-telling outright (AUP #31). The only real traffic channel is the owner pasting Naver and social posts, since automatic Naver posting risks sanctions. Other owner work: support in Korean business hours, Korean VAT registration and filing with international wires, and 통신판매업 registration past 50 transactions, which a foreign individual may be unable to complete (not verified).

ranking.candidate: cand_games: HTML5 web games on portals
ranking.reason: There is no portal API for submission or analytics, so the owner becomes the upload and metrics clerk: about 140 min/week of uploads alone at the dossier's own 35 min each, rising to 4–5 h/week (verification). CrazyGames' Basic Launch is unmonetized and gated on engagement benchmarks, so each iteration loop takes 1–3 weeks and gets little signal. Playgama rejects low-quality all-AI titles and reports AI-art games perform more than 2× worse, which hits exactly what the AI does worst: game feel and original art. The Playgama Claude plugins are SDK helpers only; they save coding time, not owner time.

recommended_strategy:
SINGLE PRODUCT, WEB-FIRST, RUN BY THE AI. Build one vertical AI practice tool as a web app inside this repo. Suggested candidate is cand_aichat niche D, reframed as the verifier suggested: 'CLB writing & speaking practice feedback' for Canadian PR and citizenship applicants. Explanations switch to Korean, Punjabi, Tagalog and other languages. It gives no official score prediction, never uses 'CELPIP' in the product name or ad text, and hard-refuses immigration and CRS questions (IRPA s.91). One flag: Anthropic's usage policy lists 'Academic testing' among high-risk uses (cross_payments). The owner must decide in week 1 whether a practice-feedback tool falls inside that. If yes, switch to another niche that passes the cross_payments category screen, such as an adult productivity or utility tool.

STACK. Next.js static pages already target Cloudflare Pages (next.config.ts). The API is a Cloudflare Worker with D1 and Sonnet 5 with a cached rubric prefix; Haiku 4.5 only caches prefixes of 4,096 tokens or more (claude-api skill). Payments go through a merchant of record (Paddle, Polar or Stripe Managed Payments), because foreign VAT applies from the first sale (cross_payments). Deploys, metric pulls and batch jobs run as GitHub Actions holding the secrets. Routines are the 'brain' that opens PRs and writes digests (cross_operator architecture).

PRICE: a hard paywall after 1 free task, then C$29/month, or a C$69 90-day pass priced below 3× monthly so the two options don't conflict (verifier). RevenueCat 2026 medians: hard paywall 10.7% vs freemium 2.1% converting by day 35.

CHANNELS: 2–3 quality-gated guide pages a week (no scaled pages); a free no-signup checker with express-consent email; and a capped Google/Microsoft search test at C$20–30/day. Kill rule: stop if cost to acquire a customer exceeds first-sale net for 14 days. Until the Ads API token is approved, the owner imports the AI-built campaign files.

WHAT THE AI DELIVERS THIS SESSION: the full codebase, payments in test mode, prompts, an eval harness, 10–15 guide pages, legal, privacy and CASL pages, ad files, Actions workflows and Routine prompts. What waits on the owner (7.25–10.75 h per the verifier): MoR KYC, Cloudflare/Anthropic/domain tokens as secrets, a virtual mailbox, legal sign-off, the ads account, the EI call, and making the public repo private.

EXPECTATIONS, stated plainly:
- ESTIMATE month-3 net C$0–1,000 base case (dossier), probably lower.
- P(averaging C$5k by Dec–Jan) well under 2% (verifier), around 1% or lower (cross_baserates).
- Cash ESTIMATE ≈ C$800–1,100 over 3 months without ads, or C$2.2–3.2k with the ad test (verifier), plus the Claude plan for Routines at US$20–200/month [prior knowledge, unverified].
- None of this can be guaranteed, and the owner needs a separate income floor.

OPTIONAL SECOND SHOT, only if setup hours remain: a Telegram Stars bot reusing the same Worker and Claude layer. Do it only after the owner confirms a TON→CAD exchange route.

notes:
I read all 15 bundle files (converted to text in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-canadian-tool-deals/f8498992-c004-57e4-9f8d-e9f9ae302e69/scratchpad/passive/judge_build/). I also read the repo's dossier INDEX, the cross_tooling conclusions and next.config.ts. Where a dossier and its verification disagreed I used the verification figures.

1) This lens favours web products because they have no human review queue between a commit and a customer. cand_aichat and cand_bots are the only two with no store or portal gatekeeper; everything else carries a human review loop or dashboard-only step.

2) Leverage is not demand. All 11 verifications cut P(C$5k by Dec–Jan) to 0.1–0.5/10. cross_baserates puts a single product at about 1% or lower. RevenueCat's ceiling (about 1 in 20 subscription apps reach $10k cumulative within 2 years) caps it below 5%. So the recommendation maximises the chance of some revenue for the least owner time. It is not a path the evidence supports to C$5k.

3) The AI cannot deploy live from this session, because egress to Stripe and Cloudflare APIs is blocked (first-hand, cross_operator). 'Launch-ready' therefore means: code, test-mode payments, content and workflows committed, waiting for the owner to add secrets or allowlist hosts. GitHub cron in this repo started 0.4–11.9 h late (n=50), and the scraper stayed 'green' through about 46 days of zero output (cross_operator). Every Routine and Action must therefore assert on outcomes and be idempotent; Routines have double-fire bugs in the CHANGELOG.

4) A hidden cost applies to every candidate: the Claude plan that runs the Routines, US$20–200/month [prior knowledge, unverified]. The daily run caps of 5 (Pro) or 15 (Max) are secondary sources.

5) The repo allforyou-bit/canadian-tool-deals is PUBLIC, including the owner's EI planning (cross_operator). The owner should make it private. A private repo gets 2,000 free Actions minutes/month on the Free plan (github/docs), which covers the lean workflow plan.

6) Legal responsibility stays with the owner under CASL (s.13 onus), PIPEDA, the Competition Act, IRPA and the EI s.30 'minor extent' test, even when the AI does all the work (cross_payments).

7) Unknowns that could flip the recommended niche:
- whether a practice-feedback tool counts as 'Academic testing' under Anthropic's usage policy;
- CELPIP cost per click, and whether trademark ad restrictions apply (not found);
- whether the merchant of record accepts an AI practice tool (Polar puts 'exam tools' under closer review).
